subject: Calibrating two LLM judges
body: A product team compared two LLM judges scoring support answers. Agreement with human raters rose from 71% to 86% after they added a three-point rubric with one anchored example per score. The biggest gains came on borderline answers, where judges had previously split.

subject: Worth reading: judge calibration
body: Our pick this week is the judge-calibration write-up. Adding a three-point rubric with anchored examples lifted judge agreement with human raters from 71% to 86%. If you run LLM-as-judge, start with the rubric before you swap models.

subject: Version your golden set like code
body: Teams that store their golden set in the repo and review label changes in pull requests catch silent eval drift. One team found 12 mislabeled cases only because a label diff showed up next to a prompt change. Treat every label edit as a reviewed change.

subject: Pairwise beats absolute scoring for tone
body: For subjective qualities like tone, pairwise comparisons gave more stable results than 1-to-5 scores. Re-running the same set gave a 4% swing with pairwise versus 15% with absolute scoring. Use absolute scores for facts and pairwise for style.

subject: How red teams build injection test sets
body: A security team built a test set of 50 prompt-injection attacks, including classic lines such as 'ignore previous instructions'. A separate screening call that ran before summarization caught 45 of the 50. Their advice: keep attack examples in your eval set and re-run them on every prompt change.

subject: Interviewers remember decision stories
body: Hiring panels recall candidates who tell decision stories: the constraint, the options, the trade-off and what they would change. In a survey of 40 interviewers, 31 said a clear trade-off mattered more than the outcome itself.

subject: What PM interviewers actually recall
body: A survey of 40 PM interviewers found that 31 valued a clearly explained trade-off over the result. Candidates who walk through constraint, options, trade-off and hindsight are the ones panels remember.

subject: Ladders that use outcomes, not scope
body: A product org rewrote its career ladder around observable outcomes instead of team size. Promotion disputes dropped by half in the first cycle because evidence was easier to check.

subject: PM pay bands: what 1,200 PMs reported
body: A survey of 1,200 product managers found equity makes up a smaller share of total pay at later-stage companies. The authors suggest negotiating scope and level before title, because level drives the pay band.

subject: AI PM loops now include an eval exercise
body: Several AI product teams have added an eval design exercise to PM interviews. Candidates get a feature brief and 30 minutes to propose test cases, a pass bar and a launch gate.

subject: A handoff checklist for agents
body: An agent team published the checklist it uses to decide when a human must take over: low confidence, an irreversible action, or a policy topic. Escalations became predictable and reviewers stopped seeing surprise actions.

subject: Link of the week: agent handoffs
body: This week's top link is a short checklist for when an agent should hand control to a human: low confidence, irreversible actions and policy topics.

subject: Ship read-only agents first
body: Teams that launched agents as read-only first, then added write actions behind a confirmation step, reported fewer rollbacks. One team shipped writes three months after GA with zero incidents.

subject: Tool-call budgets stop runaway loops
body: Capping an agent at eight tool calls per request cut timeouts by 30% with no drop in task success. Most runs that hit the cap were already stuck in a loop.

subject: Indirect prompt injection, explained
body: Attackers hide text in web pages and emails that agents read, for example a line telling the assistant to forward data. Defenses that work: treat fetched content as untrusted data, screen it before use, and allowlist the tools an agent may call.

subject: Keep a product bet ledger
body: A bet ledger lists each product bet, the assumption behind it and the evidence that would prove it wrong. Reviewing it quarterly showed one team that 40% of shipped bets had never been validated.

subject: Pricing AI features by outcome
body: B2B companies are testing outcome-based pricing for AI features, such as a price per resolved ticket instead of per seat. Early results show easier sales conversations but harder revenue forecasting.

subject: Write kill criteria before launch
body: Teams that wrote kill criteria before launch shut down failing features in a median of 6 weeks, compared with 5 months for teams that decided afterwards.

subject: Scoring platform work fairly
body: Plain RICE under-scores platform work such as permissions and audit trails because direct reach is small. Adding a multiplier for the number of roadmap items each platform item unblocks fixed the ranking for one team.

subject: The narrow wedge for vertical AI
body: Vertical AI startups that started with one painful workflow reached paid pilots faster than those selling a broad assistant. The wedge earns the data and trust needed to expand.
